text: When you build a REST API, good design matters. Start by giving your endpoints clear, meaningful names, such as /users or /orders, so developers can easily understand them. Always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Documentation is equally important, because clear guides help others use your API without confusion. You should also plan for versioning from the beginning, for example by adding /v1/ to your URLs. This way, older applications keep working when you make changes. Following these simple practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
